Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi, who is in New York to attend the annual session of the United Nations General Assembly, participated Friday in the 27th Informal Meeting of the Council of Ministers of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO), chaired by Pakistan. Araghchi thanked Pakistan and the ECO Secretariat for organizing the meeting and emphasized the importance of strengthening regional cooperation among member states. Referring to the current state of the international system, Araghchi said the meeting was being held at a time when the world is facing growing uncertainty and fragmentation, while international law and international humanitarian law are increasingly being affected by acts of aggression. Referring to the US-Zionist military aggression against Iran over the past two years, the Iranian foreign minister said the Islamic Republic of Iran, despite its firm commitment to diplomacy and negotiations, has fallen victim to the illegal, aggressive and terrorist actions of the United States and the Israeli regime. Pointing to the material and moral damage caused by the military aggression of the United States and Israel against Iran, as well as the martyrdom of the Leader of the Islamic Revolution, a number of senior military commanders, more than 4,000 Iranians, and 168 schoolchildren in the city of Minab, he added that numerous infrastructures, including hospitals, civilian airports and historic buildings, were targeted and damaged during the imposed war by the aggressors. Araghchi also referred to the resistance of Iran’s powerful armed forces and people, stressing that none of the aggressors’ sinister objectives were achieved thanks to the resistance of the Iranian people and the strength of the Armed Forces, and that Iran emerged from this historic test proud and more dignified than ever. The foreign minister went on to emphasize the Islamic Republic of Iran’s determination to enhance regional cooperation, saying Iran is committed to strengthening regional cooperation and solidarity and believes that ECO can play a more active role in promoting economic and trade cooperation, regional connectivity and sustainable development among its member states. Elsewhere in his remarks, Araghchi referred to recent developments within ECO and highlighted the resumption of several important meetings of the organization that had been suspended for several years, including ministerial meetings on trade, internal affairs and the environment. The foreign minister also cited the adoption of a five-year roadmap for cooperation in the mining sector, a 10-year strategy for sustainable and resilient transport in the ECO region, and the launch of the process to amend the ECO Trade Agreement (ECOTA) as examples of the member states’ collective determination to strengthen regional cooperation. Referring to the process of finalizing the ECO Vision for the coming decade, he expressed hope that the document would be considered and approved at the 18th ECO Summit in Tehran, with the aim of ensuring its feasibility, measurability and effective implementation. The foreign minister also described the development of transport infrastructure and regional connectivity as other important areas of cooperation among member states, saying the expansion of ECO corridors and their growing links with major freight and logistics hubs, including those connected to China, would strengthen the region’s role in international trade and transit networks. Araghchi described the growing trend of regional tourism and the expansion of intra-regional trade as signs of the gradual strengthening of the foundations of economic integration in the ECO region, while emphasizing that areas such as energy, human resources, agriculture and industry, and the environment remain among the region’s key priorities.Thanking the member states for their commitment and the efforts of the ECO Secretariat under Ambassador Majid Khan, he stressed the need to continue this process and make use of the organization’s capacities to advance the common objectives of its member states. In another part of his remarks, the foreign minister referred to the Islamic Republic of Iran’s hosting of the 18th ECO Summit in Tehran on December 3-4, 2026, emphasizing the importance of holding the summit at the highest level. Araghchi stressed that the valuable participation of the leaders of ECO member states in the summit could send an appropriate message to the peoples of the region and the international community. The foreign minister concluded by expressing hope that, through strengthened regional and multilateral cooperation, peace, security and prosperity would be further realized around the world and that unilateral coercive measures and acts of aggression that fuel instability and insecurity would come to an end.

item.title: Iranian Brunei Foreign Ministers meet on sidelines of UN General Assembly
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi and Brunei Foreign Minister Prince Abdul Mateen met on Thursday afternoon on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly. During the meeting, the two sides discussed bilateral relations and international developments, particularly issues concerning the Muslim world, including Palestine and the genocide of Palestinians. Araghchi stressed the need for the Organization of Islamic Cooperation to pay greater attention to the issue of Palestine. Referring to the intensification of the occupying regime’s crimes against Palestinians in Gaza, the West Bank, Al-Quds and other parts of the occupied Palestinian territories, as well as the regime’s continued aggression against Lebanon and other Muslim countries, he underscored the need for urgent action to counter the Zionist regime’s colonial domination. The two sides also held consultations on Iran-Brunei bilateral relations.

Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi, continuing his consultations with his counterparts attending the United Nations General Assembly session, met and held talks with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov on Thursday afternoon. During the meeting, the two sides discussed the state of bilateral cooperation in various fields, including political, economic, trade, transportation and energy affairs, as well as coordination at the level of international organizations. The Iranian foreign minister praised Russia’s responsible positions in opposing the United States’ aggressive unilateralism and its misuse of international organizations to exert pressure on independent countries. The Iranian and Russian foreign ministers also exchanged views on developments in West Asia following the United States’ repeated breaches of its commitments and its violation of the provisions of the Islamabad understanding. The Iranian foreign minister briefed his Russian counterpart on the latest status of the talks and understanding between Iran and Oman regarding the establishment of a safe maritime route through the Strait of Hormuz, as well as the continued efforts by mediators to convey the conditions and essential elements required for a return to the diplomatic process. Araghchi described the current insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz as a direct result of the United States’ failure to honor its commitments and its crimes against Iran. Recalling Iran’s goodwill throughout the negotiations that led to the understanding to end the war, he stressed that, just as the Islamic Republic of Iran demonstrated seriousness in the diplomatic arena, it remains determined to defend its national interests and security and prevent the United States from misusing the Strait of Hormuz to threaten Iran’s national security. The Russian foreign minister, reiterating his country’s principled position in condemning the US and Israeli military aggression against Iran and the efforts by the United States and its allies to instrumentally misuse international organizations to advance their objectives, stressed the importance of all countries adhering to international law and the principles of the United Nations Charter.

Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi, who has traveled to New York to attend the annual session of the United Nations General Assembly, met and held talks with British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband on Thursday afternoon on the sidelines of the session. The foreign ministers of Iran and Britain discussed bilateral relations as well as regional and international issues. The Iranian foreign minister described the insecurity in the region and the Strait of Hormuz as a consequence of the US-Israeli military aggression, which was carried out with the support and backing of some European countries and had caused extensive damage to Iran, the region and the world. The foreign minister said lasting stability and security in the region depended on ending the occupation and ensuring the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people, particularly their right to self-determination. He recalled that the British government and some other European governments must be held accountable for the role they have played in the emergence and continuation of an occupying and terrorist regime in West Asia. Araghchi called for a correction of the destructive and irresponsible approaches adopted by some European governments toward Iran and regional developments, stressing that insisting on interference in the internal affairs of countries and the instrumental use of human rights concepts is in no way acceptable. Araghchi described the continued comprehensive military and political support provided by Britain and some other European countries as a major factor contributing to the escalation of the occupying regime’s crimes against the Palestinian people and the countries of the region. He stressed that Britain and other countries are obligated under relevant international treaties to take action to prosecute and punish officials of the Israeli regime for genocide and war crimes. The foreign minister also stressed Iran’s responsible approach to using the potential of diplomacy to resolve issues related to Iran’s peaceful nuclear program, noting that the three European countries must be held accountable for following the United States’ illegal actions regarding the snapback mechanism and for failing to take a firm position against the US and Israeli military aggression against Iran’s peaceful nuclear facilities. The foreign ministers of Iran and Britain also discussed bilateral relations and diplomatic and consular consultations between the two countries.

item.title: Iranian Egyptian FMs meet in New York to discuss bilateral ties regional developments
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi, who has traveled to New York to attend the annual session of the United Nations General Assembly, met with Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty on Thursday afternoon. The two sides discussed Iran-Egypt bilateral relations and regional developments, particularly the issue of Palestine. The Iranian foreign minister highlighted the moral and international legal responsibilities of all countries, particularly Islamic countries, to stop the genocide of the Palestinian people, stating that the Palestinian issue is the greatest humanitarian and moral crisis of the contemporary world. He stressed that all countries are obliged to confront occupation and help realize the Palestinian people’s right to self-determination and the establishment of an independent Palestinian state with Al-Quds as its capital. Araghchi also referred to the Israeli regime’s aggression against Lebanon, Syria and other countries in the region, stressing the need to strengthen coordination among regional countries, including at the United Nations and the Organization of Islamic Cooperation, to counter the Israeli regime’s expansionism and assaults on the security and stability of the region. The two sides also exchanged views on strengthening Iran-Egypt relations and bilateral cooperation.

item.title: Iranian Kyrgyz Foreign Ministers meet on sidelines of UN General Assembly
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi, who has traveled to New York to attend the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, met with Kyrgyz Foreign Minister Zheenbek Kulubaev on Thursday afternoon. They exchanged views and held consultations on bilateral relations and the most important developments in Central Asia, the Caucasus and West Asia. Araghchi stressed the Islamic Republic of Iran’s determination to develop and deepen relations with Kyrgyzstan, within the framework of Iran’s approach to expanding ties with the countries of Central Asia and the Caucasus, in all areas of mutual interest. Araghchi also outlined the latest regional developments amid the continuation of the United States’ aggressive and interventionist actions, as well as its economic war against Iran, stressing that Iran would act with steadfastness and determination in defending its sovereignty, security and national interests. The foreign ministers of Iran and Kyrgyzstan also held consultations on following up on agreements reached by the two countries’ presidents and implementing bilateral understandings in various economic and trade fields.

item.title: Iranian Portuguese Foreign Ministers meet in New York discuss international bilateral issues
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi and Portuguese Foreign Minister Paulo Rangel met and held talks on Thursday afternoon on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. During the meeting, the foreign ministers of Iran and Portugal exchanged views on the most important international developments and bilateral issues of mutual interest. The Iranian foreign minister, outlining the ongoing developments in the region, said the insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz and disruption to shipping were a direct result of the aggressive actions of the United States and the Israeli regime, stressing that restoring maritime security in the region requires an end to the US’s destabilizing actions and economic terrorism. Araghchi stressed that the European Union and its member states should adopt an independent and responsible approach, in line with international law, toward developments in West Asia.

item.title: Iranian Cypriot Foreign Ministers discuss bilateral ties international issues
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi, continuing consultations with the foreign ministers of countries participating in the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, held talks with Cypriot Foreign Minister Constantinos Kombos on Thursday afternoon. The two sides discussed and exchanged views on bilateral relations and international developments. The Iranian foreign minister, outlining Iran’s positions on regional developments following the United States’ breach of its commitments and the escalation of its aggressive and destabilizing actions in the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz, stressed the need for all countries to adopt a responsible approach and refrain from any alignment with parties committing aggression and violating the law. The Cypriot foreign minister, for his part, reaffirmed Cyprus’s commitment to the principles of the UN Charter and international law. The foreign ministers of Iran and Cyprus also exchanged views on several issues of common interest concerning bilateral relations and regional affairs.

item.title: Araghchi meets Spanish FM calls for European action against US aggression
item.description: Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who is in New York to attend the annual session of the United Nations General Assembly, met and held talks with José Manuel Albares Bueno, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Spain, on Thursday morning. The Iranian Foreign Minister, outlining the ongoing developments in the West Asia region, stressed the importance of European countries adopting a responsible approach consistent with international law toward the US aggressive and unlawful actions against Iran. The Foreign Minister also, referring to the continued occupation and genocide of the Palestinians and Israel’s aggressive expansionism in the region, underscored the responsibility of all states to stop these acts of aggression and hold the Zionist perpetrators accountable and punish them. The two sides also discussed and exchanged views on bilateral relations between Iran and Spain.
